evidence: The ORCID is credited by Oxford to Donald Lateiner at Ohio Wesleyan, whose faculty CV lists The Historical Method of Herodotus and Sardonic Smile.

The 2002 thesis on civil-rights struggle in Jim Crow South Carolina leads directly into Democracy Rising (2006), on South Carolina and the fight for Black equality; the dates and specific research connect.

Berkeley confirms Ruth Marie Leacock’s 1959 dissertation on Malet-DuPan. I found no source connecting that French Revolution dissertation to the author of the Brazil books; the dates fit but the works do not establish continuity.
USP identifies this exact ORCID with Maria Cristina da Silva Leme at FAU-USP; her research-network biography identifies her as organizer of Urbanismo no Brasil 1895-1965.
Columbia’s biography of the Paris-I Latin American historian Annick Lempérière explicitly lists both Les clercs de la nation (1992) and Entre Dieu et le roi, la république (2004).
The dissertation and book have the same distinctive title, Rättvisans och allmogens beskyddare, and identical subtitle, chronological range and author; the thesis adds an English translation.
The Illiberal Reformers author was born in 1960, making the 1973 PhD impossible at age 13; the dissertation concerns American military culture rather than his history of economics.

The 1982 dissertation specifically studies public policy and social conflict in Montreal, 1960-81; The Reconquest of Montreal (1990) develops the same city’s language policy and bilingual social change at a plausible later date.

Rational Recreation is catalogued as a 1980 dissertation by Robert M. (Robert Michael) Lewis, born 1946, matching the book author’s middle initial and birth year; both works concern nineteenth-century American leisure and entertainment.
The French stadium researcher is Robert W. Lewis, whose CV records a 1998 BA and 2007 Wisconsin PhD; the American theatrical-spectacle editor is Robert M. Lewis, born 1946, at Birmingham.

The Soviet Experiment reviewer is credited at Exeter with the initials R.A. in his institutional email; Hopkins identifies the theatrical-spectacle editor as Robert M. Lewis, an American historian at Birmingham.

The Urban Harvest dissertation (1986) and Soviet Nationality Policy (1992) examine the same unusually specific topic: Soviet ethnic policy, urbanization and identity in the Ukrainian SSR during 1923-1933/34.
The 1969 dissertation and 1977 book share the exact core title Labor on the Illinois Central Railroad, 1852-1900; the later book adds a subtitle, fitting a thesis-to-book career.

The books Um grande cerco de paz and Tutela and the articles on tutela, indigenous peoples, state formation and public administration form a continuous, specifically connected research programme across the listed dates.

João Heraldo Lima’s 1981 book concerns coffee and industry in Minas Gerais; João Victor da Mota Uzer Lima’s 2024 thesis concerns US conspiracism in 1989-2016. The full given names, research subjects and career dates do not connect.
